STEP 1 - Scene: A small side salad of fresh spinach leaves with shredded carrot, on a white plate. Photographed from above at an oblique angle, with the plate tilted, so the plate looks elongated.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a white side/salad plate, roughly 20 cm across its longest undistorted width. Area ≈ 3.14 × (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2. Using the foreshortened view, the effective food-bearing area is similar.

STEP 3 - Items: Fresh spinach leaves (main item, with stems) and shredded raw carrot. No visible dressing or oil.

STEP 4 - Area: Spinach covers about 18% of the plate (~57 cm^2). Carrot shreds cover about 3% (~9 cm^2). Total food coverage ≈ 21%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Spinach: 57 cm^2 × 3 cm ≈ 171 ml (loosely piled). Carrot: 9 cm^2 × 1 cm ≈ 9 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Spinach: 171 ml × 0.15 ≈ 26 g. Carrot: 9 ml × 0.6 ≈ 5 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Spinach, raw, ~23 kcal/100 g: 26 g → 6 kcal. Carrot, raw, ~41 kcal/100 g: 5 g → 2 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest pile of leaves with a little carrot on a 20 cm plate is plausibly about 30 g and under 10 kcal. The totals are consistent with the visible amount.

Total: about 31 g, about 8 kcal.
